t: You're on King William Walk in central Greenwich, which runs north from the entrance to Greenwich Park along the edge of the Old Royal Naval College, down to the Cutty Sark and the Greenwich foot tunnel. On the western side are homes, shops, restaurants and two pubs. The eastern side has the Discover Greenwich Visitor Centre and former College buildings now used by the University of Greenwich. The street is named for William IV, King of the United Kingdom and Hanover from 1830 until 1837, and the third son of George III.
